messages.content: What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?

message.content: The common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is a small, insectivorous mammal that lived roughly 55 million years ago. This ancestor belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, the group that gave rise to many modern land mammals, including the orders Carnivora (to which lions belong) and Perissodactyla (to which zebras belong).
